title: Why the World Won’t End
spine: The book’s distributed-capability argument earns conditional hope by tracing a concrete food-system cascade, then showing why recovery needs usable knowledge and institutions capable of correction.

source.scope: Complete title note and substantive extracted sections 5, 6, 10, 11; source-9 is a fragmented heading, read with source-10. Opening portions of source-3, source-4 and source-8 plus complete chapter map and source-specific supporting paragraphs. Does not claim full word-by-word book reread or independent literature verification.
source.images: Extraction lists only cover; existing figure inventory remains. Original source-supported conceptual scenes are proposed, not quantitative diagrams.

scenes.title: What must survive
lines: Why the World Won’t End asks what lets civilization continue after devastating shocks.
Its hopeful argument begins with distributed knowledge, spare capacity, and communities that can adapt.
Failures need not erase every surviving ability to grow food, repair equipment, or cooperate.
The book separates human extinction from damaged societies that still have choices.
Readers learn to judge danger by what fails and what remains usable.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Book-first value; curiosity becomes a concrete question about remaining capabilities.
scenes.artPlan: Wide repair depot rather than symbolic world map: two materially distinct working sites, one grows food and one maintains equipment; a damaged transport link interrupts exchange while local work continues. Small held book identifies the volume only once; header remains sole heading. Camera focus shifts from interruption to work continuing at the other location. Do not imply the two sites are independent of every possible hazard.

scenes.title: After the first shock
lines: Its nuclear-war discussion follows consequences long after the first explosions end.
Soot from burning cities could reduce sunlight and damage crops far from combat.
Trade disruption could then prevent food reaching people who escaped the blasts.
A grain warehouse helps only when institutions can organize distribution and maintain transport.
This explains why the book examines coordination alongside weapons and physical destruction.
Prevention remains essential, while recovery planning addresses people who could still survive.
scenes.emotionalPlan: The opening claim meets a severe case; concern without spectacle, then practical attention.
scenes.artPlan: A spatially continuous authored food-system cross-section: distant city silhouette with restrained smoke rises into a high atmospheric soot layer, sunlight rays diminish over a cultivated field, harvested sacks become fewer without numerical scale, and a stationary truck interrupts a real route to waiting adults. Then a warehouse clerk inventories sacks and a dispatcher sends a truck along the still-usable route; do not erase the damaged field or show universal recovery. Retain conditional wording in speech, no casualty counts, blast spectacle or celebratory rescue.

scenes.title: Keep knowledge usable
lines: Knowledge alone cannot rebuild the supply chains needed to use it.
A technical manual cannot replace trained crews, working tools, and available parts.
For electrical disruption, the book asks about replaceable transformers and offline procedures.
Crews need usable instructions and equipment before they can restore essential services.
Redundancy costs money before an emergency, but can preserve function when something fails.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Discovery: stored words become useful only through maintained material and human capability.
scenes.artPlan: Large electrical-maintenance close-up, distinctly different from warehouse: technician opens a paper procedure beside an isolated failed transformer bay; initially no spare exists and the procedure alone does nothing. A kept spare arrives with another trained crew member; grounded nontechnical cable/connection depiction then makes a nearby water pump operate. This is a conceptual illustration of the book’s preparedness questions, not a verified repair protocol, historic event, or guarantee that every blackout is repairable. A stored spare remains visibly costly inventory rather than magic creation; reveal it from a maintained spare bay. No safe-operating instructions or technical circuit diagram.

scenes.title: Survival still leaves choices
lines: But the book also asks what kind of society survives those repairs.
Emergency powers can harden into control even while essential services keep running.
Its later chapters connect leadership, technology, and institutions that can admit mistakes.
The final argument asks us to preserve rights, knowledge, and ways to correct errors.
Begin with the four kinds of ending, then follow the chapter on catastrophe.
Read it to distinguish staying alive from retaining the ability to build something better.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Relief is complicated by political stakes, then an earned invitation to examine the full argument.
scenes.artPlan: Shift from equipment scale to a civic hearing: the repaired water service remains operating in a small distant foreground inset; an adult resident brings an observed service problem, and an official first turns away while an emergency-order sheet restricts questioning. Then illustrate the book’s desired alternative with the report admitted into the public record and another resident permitted to speak; this is a contrasted institutional choice, not a claim catastrophe produces democratic reform. End at a reader’s actual spread containing four concise category names and a page marker for the catastrophe chapter, with human attention and no duplicated SVG title. Reserve y<535 for all art text; captions own bottom.

evidence.quote: The same fragmentation that makes global coordination maddening may also make total failure difficult.

evidence.heading: The Politics of Not Knowing
evidence.quote: The real design problem is how to expose uncertainty, preserve dissent, aggregate knowledge, and choose the right scale of authority without turning either centralization or decentralization into an ideology.

evidence.heading: chapter therefore asks what a correction looks like when it is neither utopia nor
evidence.quote: The inheritance worth protecting is more abstract: methods for correcting error, the accumulated knowledge of science and engineering, respect for evidence, rights that constrain power, pluralism, the capacity to cooperate with strangers, and the habit of leaving future people options rather than only obligations.

evidence.heading: chapter therefore asks what a correction looks like when it is neither utopia nor
evidence.quote: Knowledge has copies. Power has competitors. Systems can reroute. People move. Technologies simplify. Communities improvise. States rebuild.

limits: No survival guarantee or numerical extinction probability.
No claim survival is humane, catastrophe teaches wisdom, or decentralized systems cannot share correlated failures.
Recovery illustration is a proposed capability chain, not a clinical/electrical operating procedure or historical measured outcome.
Nuclear soot and food impacts remain conditional; preparedness does not replace prevention.
artIdentity: Rich maritime blue, warm terracotta, maize and soft turquoise foregrounds; working infrastructure, cultivated ground, repair-scale machinery and civic interaction on flat backgrounds. Four distinct spatial compositions rather than travelling Archive boxes or repeated cards.
